chapter_name: The Mughal School of Miniature Painting
learning_objective: 🎯 Witness the grand fusion of Indian, Persian, and European art styles patronized by the powerful Mughal emperors!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Mughal art was a brilliant mix of Persian grace, Indian colors, and European realism. It was entirely a court art—created in royal workshops (ateliers) strictly for the emperors' pleasure.
Emperor Akbar loved action, history, and mythology. His atelier illustrated massive books like the 'Akbarnama' and the 'Hamzanama'. His paintings are crowded, dynamic, and full of movement.

Under Jahangir, Mughal art reached its absolute peak. He demanded extreme realism, psychological portraits, and detailed studies of rare birds, animals, and flowers. He also introduced the golden 'Halo' behind the emperor's head.

Shah Jahan loved architecture (Taj Mahal) more than painting, so art became stiff and overly decorated with gold. Aurangzeb hated art, causing artists to flee to the hills and Rajasthan, ending the Mughal golden age.

fun_activity.title: 🦅 Ustad Mansur's Zoo
fun_activity.instructions: Ustad Mansur was Jahangir's master animal painter. Find a reference photo of an eagle or a falcon. Try to draw it focusing ONLY on the intricate, realistic details of its feathers, beak, and claws, just like Mansur!

exam_tips: 📌 'Falcon on a Bird Rest' was painted by Ustad Mansur during Jahangir's reign. This is a guaranteed 1-mark question.
📌 Akbar's period = Action, crowded scenes, and historical books. Jahangir's period = Calm, extreme realism, nature, and portraits.
📌 Mention the 'European Influence' during Jahangir's time—artists started using atmospheric perspective and halos borrowed from Christian art.
quick_recap: ⭐ Mughal painting was an aristocratic court art, not a religious art.
⭐ It is a synthesis of Persian, Indian, and European styles.
⭐ Jahangir's reign is considered the zenith (highest peak) of Mughal miniature painting.
